identity_evidence.quote: A 55-year-old postmenopausal lady presented with complaints of abdominal distention and mass coming out of the vagina for the last 10 days.

attribution_limitations: The case text and the Fig. 4 caption print different depths for the same pair of ovarian masses (9 × 6 × 4 cm each versus 9 × 6 × 5 cm each).
The lactate dehydrogenase value is printed in U/ml while its normal range is printed in U/L.

The Fig. 1 caption attributes the abdominal distention to a mass and tense ascites, while the case text says no abdominal mass could be appreciated on abdominal examination (a hard fixed mass was felt per-rectally).

CT reported hypodense deposits in the liver, pancreas and gastro-oesophageal junction as likely metastasis, while per-operative palpation found no tumour deposit on the liver surface or pancreas; the CT deposits were described as subcapsular and as likely metastasis.
The discussion calls the patient immunocompromised only inside a hypothesised cause of the fistula; no cause or test of immunocompromise is stated.
The Fig. 4 caption says the bilateral adnexal masses are showing growth without saying what grew or over what interval.
The ADNEX model risks are printed as 42.8% benign, 57.2% malignant and 41% borderline, so the three percentages do not form a partition.

The abstract says interval debulking surgery was performed at exploratory laparotomy, while the main text lists total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy and appendicectomy.
